subject: Reasoning
topic: Statement and Assumptions — Implicit Assumption Identification (W11 B1)

questions.stem:
Statement: 'Please do not use the lift in case of fire.'
Assumption I: Lift usage during fire can be dangerous.
Assumption II: Fires are common in this building.
Which assumption(s) are implicit?

options.option_text: Only Assumption I is implicit
Only Assumption II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit

questions.explanation: A is correct. Assumption I (lift is dangerous during fire) is implicit — the instruction makes sense only if using the lift in a fire is hazardous (power may cut, fire may spread through shaft). Assumption II (fires are common) is NOT implicit — a precautionary notice doesn't presuppose that fires are frequent; it only prepares for the possibility.

questions.stem:
Statement: 'An advertisement: Wanted — a marketing executive with at least 5 years of experience.'
Assumption I: Experience makes candidates more capable.
Assumption II: Candidates with experience will apply for this job.
Which assumption(s) are implicit?

options.option_text: Only Assumption I is implicit
Only Assumption II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit

questions.explanation: C is correct. Assumption I is implicit — the company sets an experience threshold because it believes experienced candidates are more capable (otherwise why the requirement?). Assumption II is implicit — publishing an advertisement presupposes that suitable experienced candidates exist and will apply (otherwise the ad is pointless). Both are foundational to the action of placing the ad.

questions.stem:
Statement: 'The government has decided to build more hospitals in rural areas.'
Assumption I: Rural areas currently have inadequate healthcare facilities.
Assumption II: All rural residents will use these hospitals.
Which assumption(s) are implicit?

options.option_text: Only Assumption I is implicit
Only Assumption II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit

questions.explanation: A is correct. Assumption I is implicit — the decision to build MORE hospitals implies that the existing facilities are insufficient. Without this assumption, the action would have no justification. Assumption II is NOT implicit — the statement says 'build hospitals', not 'all residents will use them'. One does not need to assume 100% uptake; it is sufficient that some residents will benefit.

questions.stem:
Statement: 'Buy one shirt, get one free — limited time offer!'
Assumption I: Customers are more likely to buy when they get something free.
Assumption II: The shop has surplus stock to give away.
Which assumption(s) are implicit?

options.option_text: Only Assumption I is implicit
Only Assumption II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit

questions.explanation: A is correct. Assumption I is implicit — running a 'buy one get one' promotion only makes sense if the shop expects customers to be attracted by the free offer, i.e., free items motivate purchases. Assumption II is NOT implicit — the shop may be offering from regular stock, passing on a discount, or using a supplier promotion. The existence of 'surplus stock' is not a necessary assumption for the offer to work.

questions.stem:
Statement: 'Early to bed and early to rise makes a man healthy, wealthy, and wise.'
Assumption I: A healthy routine contributes to success.
Assumption II: People who sleep late cannot be wise.
Which assumption(s) are implicit?

options.option_text: Only Assumption I is implicit
Only Assumption II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit

questions.explanation: A is correct. Assumption I is implicit — the proverb suggests a routine (early sleeping and waking) leads to positive outcomes, implying that disciplined habits promote health and success. Assumption II is NOT implicit — the statement doesn't deny wisdom to late risers; it only states that early rising contributes positively. It is an extreme generalisation not warranted by the statement.

questions.stem:
Statement: 'Children under 12 must be accompanied by an adult in the swimming pool.'
Assumption I: Children under 12 may not be able to swim safely without supervision.
Assumption II: Adults are always good swimmers.
Which assumption(s) are implicit?

options.option_text: Only Assumption I is implicit
Only Assumption II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit

questions.explanation: A is correct. Assumption I is implicit — requiring adult accompaniment assumes young children face safety risks without supervision. Assumption II is NOT implicit — the rule doesn't assume adults are skilled swimmers; it only requires their presence as a supervisory measure (an adult who cannot swim can still call for help or watch the child).

questions.stem:
Statement: 'The railway ministry has decided to introduce new express trains on the Delhi–Mumbai route.'
Assumption I: There is sufficient demand for faster connectivity between Delhi and Mumbai.
Assumption II: All existing trains on the route are overloaded.
Which assumption(s) are implicit?

options.option_text: Only Assumption I is implicit
Only Assumption II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit

questions.explanation: A is correct. Assumption I is implicit — the ministry would not introduce new express trains without expecting sufficient passenger demand on the route. Assumption II is NOT implicit — the decision to add new trains doesn't require that ALL existing trains are overloaded. New trains could be introduced for operational reasons, speed improvements, or to serve demand that current timing or capacity doesn't meet.

questions.stem:
Statement: 'Wear a helmet while riding a motorcycle.'
Assumption I: Helmets can reduce the severity of head injuries.
Assumption II: All motorcycle riders are prone to accidents.
Which assumption(s) are implicit?

options.option_text: Only Assumption I is implicit
Only Assumption II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit

questions.explanation: A is correct. Assumption I is implicit — the instruction to wear a helmet presupposes that helmets provide protection (reduce injury severity in case of an accident). Without this, the advice would be meaningless. Assumption II is NOT implicit — the advice is precautionary and does not assume that every rider WILL have an accident; it only prepares for the possibility. Saying 'all riders are prone' is an overgeneralisation not implied by a safety precaution.

questions.stem:
Statement: 'More than 90% of successful IAS officers read English newspapers daily.'
Assumption I: Reading English newspapers contributes to IAS success.
Assumption II: Only English newspaper readers can become IAS officers.
Which assumption(s) are implicit?

options.option_text: Only Assumption I is implicit
Only Assumption II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit

questions.explanation: A is correct. Assumption I is implicit — the statement is presented as a relevant fact, implying a causal/correlational link between newspaper reading and success. Assumption II is NOT implicit — the statement says 'more than 90%' (not 100%), and even that data doesn't mean only English newspaper readers can succeed; the remaining 10% are successful without reading English newspapers.

questions.stem:
Statement: 'A notice: Drinking water is available on the second floor.'
Assumption I: People in the building need drinking water.
Assumption II: The water on the second floor is safe to drink.
Which assumption(s) are implicit?

options.option_text: Only Assumption I is implicit
Only Assumption II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit

questions.explanation: C is correct. Assumption I is implicit — putting up a notice directing people to drinking water assumes that the people in the building require drinking water (otherwise there is no point in the notice). Assumption II is also implicit — the notice specifically identifies water as 'drinking water', which carries the implicit claim that it is safe for human consumption. Both assumptions underlie the purpose and meaning of the notice.
